## Amazon RDS: Automated Backups vs. Manual Snapshots

### Automated Backups
- **Managed by RDS automatically** — enabled by default when you set a backup retention period greater than 0.
- **How they work:** RDS performs a full daily storage-volume snapshot during your configured **backup window**, and continuously captures transaction logs.
- **Point-in-time recovery (PITR):** Because transaction logs are retained, you can restore to any specific second within your retention period (typically up to the last ~5 minutes before the current time).
- **Lifecycle tied to the DB instance:** Automated backups are deleted when you delete the DB instance (unless you choose to retain them), and they roll off automatically as they age out of the retention window.
- **Cost:** Backup storage up to the size of your provisioned DB storage is generally free; beyond that incurs charges.

### Manual Snapshots
- **Created on demand by you** (via console, CLI, API, or automation) — or via policies you define.
- **How they work:** A full snapshot of the storage volume at the moment you take it. They do **not** support point-in-time recovery — you can only restore to the exact moment the snapshot was taken.
- **Lifecycle controlled by you:** Manual snapshots **persist until you explicitly delete them**. They are *not* removed when the DB instance is deleted, which makes them ideal for long-term archival, compliance retention, or preserving a known-good state.
- **Cost:** Billed for the full snapshot storage.

### Retention of Automated Backups
- **Configurable range:** **0 to 35 days.**
  - Setting the retention period to **0 disables** automated backups.
  - The **default is typically 7 days** when you create a DB instance via the console (1 day via CLI/API/CloudFormation).
  - The **maximum is 35 days** for standard automated backups.
- Need to keep a backup longer than 35 days? Take a **manual snapshot** (retained indefinitely) or use the **automated backups replication / exported snapshots** mechanisms.

### Quick Comparison

| Aspect | Automated Backups | Manual Snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| Who creates them | RDS (automatically) | You (on demand) |
| Point-in-time recovery | ✅ Yes | ❌ No (snapshot moment only) |
| Retention | 0–35 days (configurable) | Until you delete them |
| Deleted with DB instance | Yes (by default) | No |
| Best for | Operational recovery, PITR | Long-term archival, compliance |

**Note:** Amazon Aurora differs slightly — its backup retention is also 1–35 days, but it uses continuous backup to Amazon S3 and the backups don't impact DB performance in the same way as standard RDS.
